subject: Biology
description: Excretion organs, kidney structure, nephron, urine formation

questions.stem: The functional UNIT of the kidney is the:

options.option_text: Glomerulus, only one part of nephron

questions.explanation: NEPHRON — basic structural + functional unit of kidney. Each kidney has ~1 MILLION nephrons. Parts: GLOMERULUS (capillary tuft) inside BOWMAN'S CAPSULE (cup-shaped); PCT (proximal convoluted tubule); LOOP OF HENLE (descending + ascending limbs, in medulla); DCT (distal CT); COLLECTING DUCT (multiple nephrons join here, drain into renal pelvis → ureter → bladder).

questions.stem: The MAIN nitrogenous waste excreted by humans (in urine) is:
questions.explanation: Humans + most mammals = UREOTELIC (excrete UREA). Why: protein metabolism gives NH₃ (toxic, water-soluble). Liver converts NH₃ → urea (less toxic, water-soluble) via UREA CYCLE (Krebs-Henseleit). Kidney filters urea → urine. Other patterns: AMMONOTELIC = ammonia (fish — flush directly into water); URICOTELIC = uric acid (birds, reptiles — saves water, important for laying eggs in dry environments — uric acid is the white part of bird droppings). Distractor 4 — creatinine is also excreted but less in quantity (used clinically as a kidney-function marker).

questions.stem: GLOMERULAR FILTRATION (first step in urine formation) is essentially:
questions.explanation: GLOMERULAR FILTRATION — high-pressure capillary blood pushed through GLOMERULUS into BOWMAN'S CAPSULE. PASSIVE: just pressure-driven (~55 mm Hg in glomerulus vs ~15 in capsule); pressure gradient pushes water + small solutes (glucose, salts, urea) into tubule. KEEPS in blood: cells (RBCs, WBCs), large proteins. GFR (Glomerular Filtration Rate) ~125 mL/min = ~180 L/day filtered! But ~99% reabsorbed → ~1.5 L urine/day. Subsequent steps: PCT reabsorption (most water + nutrients), Loop of Henle (water + salt; counter-current), DCT + collecting duct (fine adjustment).

questions.stem: DIALYSIS is a medical procedure used when:

options.option_text: Kidneys fail to filter blood properly

questions.explanation: DIALYSIS — artificial blood filtration when KIDNEYS fail (renal failure). Two types: HEMODIALYSIS — blood pumped through dialyzer (artificial membrane); urea, creatinine etc. diffuse out into dialysate; clean blood returned. Done at hospital ~3 times/week, ~4 hours each. PERITONEAL DIALYSIS — peritoneum (abdominal lining) used as natural membrane; dialysate fluid in abdomen, then drained. Can be done at home daily. DEFINITIVE treatment = KIDNEY TRANSPLANT. India has growing dialysis demand; PMNDP (PM Dialysis Program) provides free service.

questions.explanation: Normal urine pH ~6 (slightly acidic). Range: 4.5-8 (varies with diet, hydration, exercise). Diet effects: high protein (meat) → more acidic; vegetarian diet → more alkaline. Acidosis (low blood pH) → kidney secretes more H⁺, urine more acidic. Other normal traits: yellow (urochrome from bilirubin breakdown), 1.5 L/day, ~95% water + 5% solutes (urea, salts, creatinine). Abnormal: red (blood, beetroot), brown (bilirubin → liver issue), foamy (protein → kidney issue), sweet smell (diabetes — glucose in urine).

questions.stem: ADH (anti-diuretic hormone, vasopressin) acts on the kidney to:
questions.explanation: ADH (Anti-Diuretic Hormone, also called Vasopressin) — released by POSTERIOR PITUITARY when body is dehydrated. Acts on COLLECTING DUCTS of nephron → increases water permeability (via aquaporin channels) → MORE WATER REABSORBED → less + more concentrated (darker) urine. Caffeine + ALCOHOL inhibit ADH → frequent urination, dehydration. DIABETES INSIPIDUS = ADH deficiency → produce huge amounts of dilute urine (5-20 L/day!). Different from DIABETES MELLITUS (sugar) where urine is sweet with glucose.

questions.stem: On average, a HUMAN BODY has how many kidneys?
questions.explanation: TWO kidneys, one each side of vertebral column at lumbar level (~T12-L3). RIGHT KIDNEY is slightly LOWER than left (because of liver above). Bean-shaped, ~10-12 cm long, ~150 g each. ~25% of cardiac output (~1.2 L/min) flows through them — kidneys filter ALL the body's blood ~60 times/day. Can survive on ONE kidney (organ donor; born with one — about 1 in 1000). KIDNEY DISEASES — hypertension (kidneys regulate BP via RAAS), diabetes (high BS damages glomeruli), CKD (chronic kidney disease). India: TN, AP, Maharashtra are kidney transplant hubs.
